Entire's CLI is the source of truth for its own usage. Do not guess flags or
subcommands — read them from this command. You are already inside the repo:
entire auto-detects it from the git origin remote, so never ask the user for the
repo name. Pass --repo only to target a DIFFERENT repo.
Trails are project-scoped. Trail listing requires an explicit --project (--repo only filters within it), or --mine for your trails across projects.

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-vscode  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

When to use entire — the commands that bear on the work:
  checkpoint  Inspect and search checkpoints
                read-only except: delete, explain, push
  search      Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
                read-only
  session     Manage agent sessions tracked by Entire
                read-only except: adopt, attach, resume, stop
  status      Show Entire status
                read-only
  trail       Manage trails across repositories and branches

    login · logout · org · plugin · project · repo · service-account

entire search — Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using hybrid search (semantic + keyword),
powered by the Entire search service.

Requires authentication via 'entire login' (GitHub device flow).

By default, results are scoped to the current repository. Use --all-repos to
search across all accessible repos.

Run without arguments to open an interactive search. Results are
displayed in an interactive table. Use --json for machine-readable output,
and add --compact for a trimmed per-result shape suited to agents (implies
--json): id, type, repo, branch, author, date, files touched, score, match
snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (repo hits add
description and checkpoint count). Fetch full detail
for a single result with 'entire checkpoint explain <id>', or add --full to
that command to pull the checkpoint's entire session transcript. For a
checkpoint or commit hit from another repo, add --repo gh/<owner>/<repo> for
a GitHub mirror or --repo et/<project>/<repo> for an Entire-native repo. The
forge prefix is required, and the hit's id must be a full checkpoint ID (12-char hex or 26-char ULID) or a full commit SHA
(a SHA is resolved to its checkpoint by that repo's Entire API). Prefixes
cannot be resolved in another repo. This is unrelated to this command's
--repo filter below.

CLI queries also support inline filters like author:<name>, date:<week|month>,
branch:<name>, repo:<owner/name>, and repo:* to search all accessible repos.

Examples:
entire search "retry backoff" --json
  entire search "retry backoff" --json --compact
  entire search "auth timeout author:alice date:week"
  entire search --code "parseToken"

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-vscode  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --all-repos[=true|false]        Search all accessible repos instead of just the current one
      --author string                 Filter by author name
      --branch string                 Filter by branch name
      --case-sensitive[=true|false]   Case-sensitive code search (only with --code)
      --code[=true|false]             Search code content across repositories
      --compact[=true|false]          Trimmed JSON output for agents: id, repo, files touched, score, match snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (implies --json)
      --date string                   Filter by time period (week or month)
      --json[=true|false]             Output as JSON
      --limit int                     Maximum number of results (per page for checkpoint search, total for --code) (default 10)
      --page int                      Page number (1-based) (default 1)
      --repo strings                  Filter by repository (gh/owner/repo, et/proj/repo, owner/repo, ULID, or *); repeatable and comma-separated for multiple repos

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Exit code 1
entire enable — Enable Entire in current repository
Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.

Existing git hooks are kept: each is moved to <hook>.pre-entire and runs after
Entire's hook.

If the current directory is not a git repository, Entire can initialize one
for you and create an initial commit. It never creates or pushes to a remote —
publish the repository yourself when you're ready.

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-vscode  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path[=true|false]   Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --agent string                          Agent to set up hooks for (e.g., antigravity, claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, factoryai-droid, opencode, pi; external agents on $PATH are also available). Enables non-interactive mode.
      --agent-help-skill[=true|false]         Install the stable Entire agent-help skill (points agents at entire agent-help) for selected agent(s)
      --checkpoint-backend string             Checkpoint storage backend: refs (default; one git ref per checkpoint) or branch (legacy shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-push-remote string         Git remote for checkpoint uploads (saved to .entire/settings.local.json, even with --project)
      --checkpoint-remote string              Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format; providers: github, gitlab (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force[=true|false]                    Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)
      --import-history[=true|false]           During first-time setup, import the selected agents' existing session history (last 30 days) without prompting
      --init-repo[=true|false]                If not a git repo, initialize one non-interactively
      --initial-commit-message string         Commit message for the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --local[=true|false]                    Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --no-init-repo[=true|false]             If not a git repo, exit instead of prompting to initialize one
      --project[=true|false]                  Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --search-skill[=true|false]             Install the optional Entire search skill for selected agent(s)
      --skip-initial-commit[=true|false]      Don't create the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --skip-push-sessions[=true|false]       Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --telemetry[=true|false]                Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)
  -y, --yes[=true|false]                      Accept all defaults without prompting (in a non-repo directory: init git and commit; then enable all agents and accept telemetry). In an existing repository it lists the configuration files to commit rather than committing them. Does not import existing agent history — see --import-history

content.content:
Exit code 1
entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, repository
context, docs, history, code-index records, and durable memories, then exposes
retrieval, verification, and evaluation surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Set up the brain & agents:
  setup              Build the brain and start background updates
  add                Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain
  agent-guide        Preview repository-specific agent instructions
  webhook            Notify another service when this brain changes
  config             Inspect or initialize plugin configuration

Search & explore the brain:
  overview           Summarize the project, its structure, and decisions
  brief              Gather relevant context for a task
  query              Search the brain (BM25 lexical ranking)
  get                Fetch a brain item by ID
  multi-get          Fetch multiple brain items by ID
  dash               Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard

Durable memories & patterns:
  recall             Retrieve durable memories matching a query for the current branch
  remember           Record a durable memory about this repository
  distill            Extract durable memories from sessions (requires an agent)
  memories           Inspect, retract, and garbage-collect durable memories
  connect            Bind this repository to its hosted brain explicitly
  disconnect         Stop syncing this repository with its hosted brain
  verify             Verify durable memory anchors against local retained sources
  patterns           Inspect and rebuild recurring patterns from sessions

Code index & context:
  inspect            Explore code, dependencies, and change history
  show               Show one code-index record
  viz                Explore the brain as a graph in your browser

Brain state & maintenance:
  status             Show brain coverage, freshness, and workspace state
  stats              Show brain record counts and breakdowns

Workspaces & sharing:
  workspace          Manage local multi-repo brain workspaces
  bundle             Import or export local brain bundles

Troubleshooting & operations:
  memories import    Import durable memories from another memory tool's export
  memories sync      Sync this branch's local memories with the team's hosted memory set
  memories gc        Prune retracted and old superseded memories; report orphans
  memories vitality  Show serve receipts per memory (which memories the read surfaces actually emitted)
  memory             Manage conversation indexing and background jobs
  entities           Find checkpoints and sessions that changed a symbol
  repair             Rebuild Graph's committed-tree code index
  docs               Inspect how non-code documents are read into the brain
  refresh            Create or refresh the repository brain
  watch              Keep the brain up to date automatically
  stop               Pause background brain work on this machine
  start              Resume background brain work paused by `stop`
  reset              Remove local generated brain data
  repo-identity      Find and resolve conflicting brain stores

Miscellaneous:
  path               Print the persistent brain path for a repo path or URL
  capabilities       List supported features and retrieval sources
  doctor             Diagnose environment and brain pipeline problems
  version            Print plugin version
  help               Help about any command

Flags:
  -h, --help       help for entire-brain
      --help-all   List all commands, including hidden commands
  -v, --version    version for entire-brain

Use "entire-brain [command] --help" for more information about a command.

connect binds this repository to its hosted brain: it records the repo id and
API base URL (non-secrets only — the host CLI's own login mints a fresh token
per sync), then runs one immediate sync so the first pull happens right away.

Running connect (or the onboarding flow) is the ONLY way a repository starts
syncing: by default memories stay local and background triggers never connect
a repo on their own. Placement resolves through the host CLI (entire repo
view); pass --repo-id and --api-url to bypass resolution — a non-default cell
or a staging target. Re-running connect re-joins after 'entire brain
disconnect'.

Usage:

  -h, --help             help for connect

content.content:
setup is the one command that makes a repository's brain useful and keeps it
that way. It runs three phases:

  1. instant   build the deterministic core (code index, sessions,
               repository context, docs, history). Blocking, seconds, spends NO
               agent tokens. The brain is queryable the moment this returns.
  2. backfill  distill past sessions into durable facts, NEWEST FIRST, detached
               in the background on a cheap model. Spends tokens; bounded by
               --backfill-budget and the persisted distill cache, and skipped
               entirely when no agent CLI is available.
  3. daemon    register the repo into a workspace and install ONE machine-wide
               watcher service (launchd on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux)
               so freshness never depends on remembering to run anything.
               ONE means one: the installed unit is identical for every repo and
               every workspace, and each workspace's interval, distill cadence,
               agent, model, effort and session cap live in a machine-level watch
               plan the running watcher re-reads. Setting up a second repo adds a
               row to that plan; it does not rewrite, restart or steal the
               watcher the first repo is relying on.

TOKEN SPEND: phases 2 and 3 call an agent. Background distillation has a
recurring cost, bounded by five gates: the fact phase ASKS before it spends
(default no, and a run with no terminal never spends unless --yes is passed), --backfill-budget sessions per
background pass, one gated agent run per --distill-every per repo, the
persisted distill cache (a session is never distilled twice), and the cheap
--model/--effort. Passing --no-backfill with --no-daemon spends nothing at all,
and "entire brain status" reports what the backfill has done so far and whether the
watcher is alive.

EXIT CODE: setup exits 0 whenever the brain is QUERYABLE, and queryable means
it can answer: at least one of the code index, the repository context or the
history index built. Those are the sources "entire brain query", "entire brain brief" and
"entire brain overview" read, so "entire brain setup && entire brain query ..." cannot proceed on a
brain that has nothing to answer from. A component that fails without costing
that (a doc index, an entity index, a stale code index beside repository context
that built) is reported as one line, skipped, and the remaining components, the
backfill, the workspace registration and the daemon install all still run;
"entire brain status" then shows that component as failed and "entire brain doctor" prints
the reason. setup exits non-zero when nothing usable exists: the brain
directory cannot be built, every component failed, the worktree is too dirty to
index, or the repository has no commits yet.

Re-running setup is safe: it detects the existing workspace membership and
daemon instead of duplicating them, resumes rather than restarts a backfill
that is still running, and keeps whatever --interval/--distill-every/--model/
--effort the previous run was given unless you pass the flag again.

Usage:
  entire-brain setup [path] [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string             Agent for the background backfill: auto, none, codex, claude-code (default "auto")
      --agent-hooks              Merge the Claude Code PreToolUse entry even if a previous run declined it
      --backfill                 Start the background fact backfill even if a previous run declined it (SPENDS TOKENS)
      --backfill-budget int      Cap sessions the background backfill distills in one pass, newest first (0 = explicitly unlimited: the WHOLE corpus in one spend) (default 25)
      --daemon                   Install the background watcher even if a previous run declined it
      --distill-every duration   Minimum interval between the daemon's gated agent runs (default 24h0m0s)
      --effort string            Reasoning effort for the background backfill (default "low")
  -h, --help                     help for setup
      --interval duration        Daemon poll interval (default 5m0s)

Install the coding-agent guide into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md

Usage:
  entire graph setup [--repo path] [--strict | --normal] [--no-claude-hook]

Writes one shared operating guide and managed AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md references. Preserves repository Graph/Brain activation and the saved guidance mode. --strict saves mandatory tool-use rules for all enabled products; --normal resets to normal guidance. New repositories default to normal.

Also registers a Claude Code SubagentStart hook (entire graph hook claude-subagent-start) in the per-user, untracked .claude/settings.local.json, merged into existing settings and added once. Claude Code's Explore and Plan subagents do not load CLAUDE.md; the hook gives them the graph directive. --no-claude-hook skips it.

Flags:
  --repo <path>      Repository to install into (default: current repo)
  --strict           Save strict guidance for all enabled products (exclusive with --normal)
  --normal           Save normal guidance for all enabled products (exclusive with --strict)
  --no-claude-hook   Do not register the Claude Code SubagentStart hook in .claude/settings.local.json

Examples:
  entire graph setup --repo .

entire plugin — Manage Entire plugins (install, list, upgrade, search, remove)
Manage Entire plugins.

Plugins are external executables named 'entire-<name>'. The CLI discovers
plugins on $PATH and from a per-user managed directory which is
auto-prepended to PATH at startup. The managed directory is, in order of
precedence:

  $ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR/bin (override)
  $XDG_DATA_HOME/entire/plugins/bin (Linux/macOS, when set)
  ~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin (Linux/macOS default)
  %LOCALAPPDATA%\entire\plugins\bin (Windows, when set)
  ~\AppData\Local\entire\plugins\bin (Windows fallback when LOCALAPPDATA is unset)

Install sources:
  entire plugin install run                                    index lookup
  entire plugin install https://github.com/entireio/entire-run repository URL
  entire plugin install ./dist/entire-run                      local executable

Remote installs resolve the newest semver tag over the git protocol, then
download the platform's release asset (verified against the release's
checksums.txt when published). Discovery uses a git-synced plugin index;
see 'entire plugin search' and 'entire plugin index update'.

entire checkpoint — Inspect and search checkpoints
Operations on checkpoints — the persistent records of agent work tied to commits.

Commands:
  list     List checkpoints on the current branch
  explain  Explain a checkpoint, commit, or session
  tokens   Show token usage and optimization recommendations
  search   Search checkpoints (semantic + keyword)
  delete   Delete a checkpoint locally and from checkpoint remotes

Examples:
  entire checkpoint list
  entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>
  entire checkpoint tokens <id>
  entire checkpoint search "fix login"
  entire checkpoint delete <id> --dry-run

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-vscode  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Subcommands: delete · explain · list · push · search · tokens
             read-only except: delete, explain, push
Next:  entire agent-help checkpoint <subcommand>

#####
entire checkpoint search — Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using hybrid search (semantic + keyword),
powered by the Entire search service.

Requires authentication via 'entire login' (GitHub device flow).

By default, results are scoped to the current repository. Use --all-repos to
search across all accessible repos.

Run without arguments to open an interactive search. Results are
displayed in an interactive table. Use --json for machine-readable output,
and add --compact for a trimmed per-result shape suited to agents (implies
--json): id, type, repo, branch, author, date, files touched, score, match
snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (repo hits add
description and checkpoint count). Fetch full detail
for a single result with 'entire checkpoint explain <id>', or add --full to
that command to pull the checkpoint's entire session transcript. For a
checkpoint or commit hit from another repo, add --repo gh/<owner>/<repo> for
a GitHub mirror or --repo et/<project>/<repo> for an Entire-native repo. The
forge prefix is required, and the hit's id must be a full checkpoint ID (12-char hex or 26-char ULID) or a full commit SHA
(a SHA is resolved to its checkpoint by that repo's Entire API). Prefixes
cannot be resolved in another repo. This is unrelated to this command's
--repo filter below.

CLI queries also support inline filters like author:<name>, date:<week|month>,
branch:<name>, repo:<owner/name>, and repo:* to search all accessible repos.

Examples:
entire checkpoint search "retry backoff" --json
  entire checkpoint search "retry backoff" --json --compact
  entire checkpoint search "auth timeout author:alice date:week"
  entire checkpoint search --code "parseToken"

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-vscode  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --all-repos[=true|false]        Search all accessible repos instead of just the current one
      --author string                 Filter by author name
      --branch string                 Filter by branch name
      --case-sensitive[=true|false]   Case-sensitive code search (only with --code)
      --code[=true|false]             Search code content across repositories
      --compact[=true|false]          Trimmed JSON output for agents: id, repo, files touched, score, match snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (implies --json)
      --date string                   Filter by time period (week or month)
      --json[=true|false]             Output as JSON
      --limit int                     Maximum number of results (per page for checkpoint search, total for --code) (default 10)
      --page int                      Page number (1-based) (default 1)
      --repo strings                  Filter by repository (gh/owner/repo, et/proj/repo, owner/repo, ULID, or *); repeatable and comma-separated for multiple repos

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

input.description: Explore views data loading
input.prompt:
Repository: /Users/abhi/Documents/entire-vscode (a VS Code extension, TypeScript, for the Entire CLI). Read-only exploration, thoroughness "very thorough". The repo guide asks agents to locate code with `entire graph query --repo . --profile full --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --query "<task>"` and callers with `entire graph neighbors --repo . --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --symbol <Name> --direction in`; use those for locating symbols, and Read for source.

Goal: we are planning to add SEARCH over sessions, checkpoints, and trails in this extension. I need a precise map of how the three tree views load and render data today, so the plan can reuse it. Report, with file:line references:

1. src/ext/views/checkpointsTree.ts, sessionsTree.ts, trailsTree.ts, nodes.ts, rowRegistry.ts, scrollLoader.ts, selectionSync.ts: the Node union type and its kinds, how each tree builds children, the `paged(...)` helper and LISTS constants, how "load more" works, how contextValue strings are built (e.g. `web`, `openable`, `hasCommit`), and how clicking a row opens the detail panel (commands entire.openDetail etc.).
2. src/ext/repoManager.ts: RepoContext shape, the viewState machine (noFolder/notGit/cliMissing/cliTooOld/notEnabled/ready), how it sets VS Code context keys (entire.viewState, entire.trailsState, entire.hasTrails, entire.hasWebRepo, entire.trailsFilter), how checkpoints, sessions (local + remote "moreSessionsOnEntire"), and trails are fetched and cached, what data types they hold (SessionEntry, checkpoint entry, trail entry), any existing filter (trails filter, filterTrails command).
3. src/core/entireCli.ts and src/core/schemas.ts: every CLI invocation the extension makes (args), the Result type, how JSON is parsed/validated (zod or hand-rolled?), and the version gate (0.12.0). Is there already any call to `entire search` or `entire checkpoint search`? Also src/core/remoteSessions.ts and src/core/trails.ts and src/core/checkpointIndex.ts: what they do.
4. src/ext/commands.ts and src/extension.ts: how commands are registered, and the pattern for quick picks (e.g., filterTrails) — I want to know whether there's an existing QuickPick pattern to reuse for a search UI.
5. src/ext/panel/panelController.ts / panelManager.ts / trailPanelController.ts: what inputs open a checkpoint, session, or trail detail panel (e.g., by checkpoint id, session id, trail number), so search results can open them.
6. Tests: test/unit/support.ts, test/fake-entire/entire (the fake CLI used in integration tests: how it dispatches subcommands and fixtures), test/helpers/fixtureRepo.ts, and one integration test (e.g., test/integration/trails.test.cjs) to show the pattern. package.json scripts for test/lint/build.

Return a concise but complete report (max ~1200 words) with the key type signatures quoted verbatim where short.

input.description: Explore setup and brain state
input.prompt:
Repository: /Users/abhi/Documents/entire-vscode (a VS Code extension, TypeScript, for the Entire CLI). Read-only exploration, thoroughness "very thorough". The repo guide asks agents to locate code with `entire graph query --repo . --profile full --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --query "<task>"` and callers with `entire graph neighbors --repo . --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --symbol <Name> --direction in`; use those for locating symbols, and Read for source.

Goal: we are planning an "Entire Setup" flow in the extension for repositories where Entire isn't set up: install CLI, `entire login`, `entire enable`, Graph plugin (`entire graph setup`), Brain plugin (`entire brain setup`), and `entire brain connect` for repos hosted on Entire. I need a precise map of what already exists. Report, with file:line references:

1. src/core/cliLocator.ts: how the CLI is found (PATH, setting `entire.cliPath`?), what version is required, and src/ext/commands.ts handlers for entire.installCli, entire.setCliPath, entire.copyEnableCommand, entire.copyLoginCommand, entire.copyBrainInstallCommand, entire.copyBrainSetupCommand — what each does exactly (copies to clipboard? opens terminal? opens URL?). Is there any existing code that runs a command in a VS Code integrated terminal (vscode.window.createTerminal / sendText)?
2. src/ext/repoManager.ts: how it decides `notEnabled` (which CLI call or file check, e.g. `entire status --json`, `.entire/settings.json`), how it detects login state (trailsState 'loggedOut' / 'noAccess'), how it detects whether the repo is hosted on Entire (entire.hasWebRepo, webLinks), and any `entire repo view` / `auth status` calls.
3. Brain: src/core/brain.ts, src/core/brainPage.ts, src/ext/brainService.ts, src/ext/views/brainView.ts, src/core/serverProcess.ts. How does the extension detect whether the brain plugin is installed, whether the brain is set up for the repo, and whether it's hosted/connected? What states does the Brain webview show (e.g., "install plugin", "run setup")? Quote the state enum/type. What does `entire brain status --json` parsing look like, if any? Does anything detect the graph plugin?
4. src/core/exec.ts and src/core/errors.ts: how child processes are run (timeouts, cancellation, env), and how errors are classified (e.g., not logged in, not found, too old).
5. src/core/webLinks.ts: how a repo's entire.com URL is derived from git remotes; does it know gh/ vs et/ forges?
6. package.json: the `contributes.configuration` section (settings), the viewsWelcome entries for notEnabled/cliMissing/cliTooOld/loggedOut, activationEvents, and any walkthroughs (contributes.walkthroughs). Also README.md sections that describe setup.
7. Tests touching these: test/unit/cliLocator.test.ts, test/unit/brain.test.ts, test/integration/states.test.cjs, test/integration/brain.test.cjs, and test/fake-entire/entire (how it fakes `status`, `brain`, `auth`, version, etc., and env vars that control fake behaviour).

Return a concise but complete report (max ~1200 words) with key type signatures and state names quoted verbatim.

2. src/ext/repoManager.ts: how it decides `notEnabled` (which CLI call or file check, e.g. `entire status --json`, `.entire/settings.json`), how it detects login state (trailsState 'loggedOut' / 'noAccess'), how it detects whether the repo is hosted on Entire (entire.hasWebRepo, webLinks), and any `entire repo view` / `auth status` calls.
3. Brain: src/core/brain.ts, src/core/brainPage.ts, src/ext/brainService.ts, src/ext/views/brainView.ts, src/core/serverProcess.ts. How does the extension detect whether the brain plugin is installed, whether the brain is set up for the repo, and whether it's hosted/connected? What states does the Brain webview show (e.g., "install plugin", "run setup")? Quote the state enum/type. What does `entire brain status --json` parsing look like, if any? Does anything detect the graph plugin?
4. src/core/exec.ts and src/core/errors.ts: how child processes are run (timeouts, cancellation, env), and how errors are classified (e.g., not logged in, not found, too old).
5. src/core/webLinks.ts: how a repo's entire.com URL is derived from git remotes; does it know gh/ vs et/ forges?
6. package.json: the `contributes.configuration` section (settings), the viewsWelcome entries for notEnabled/cliMissing/cliTooOld/loggedOut, activationEvents, and any walkthroughs (contributes.walkthroughs). Also README.md sections that describe setup.

Report committed-tree indexing health, including healthy results

Usage:
  entire graph health [--repo path] [--json] [--refresh]

Reports unique flagged source files, percentages, the inclusive 5% degradation threshold, language and diagnostic breakdowns, affected files and parser diagnostic locations. Documentation, configuration and data do not dilute the source denominator. Intentional skips are listed separately; stronger unsafe and unusable-graph safeguards still apply. Parser limitations do not establish invalid source code.

Defaults to committed HEAD and the full profile. Reuses a matching index or builds one, announcing the build on stderr. --refresh rebuilds and invalidates derived query caches. Older health calculations are invalidated by cache versioning. Matching means the same tree, profile, provider and indexing policy; it does not include uncommitted source edits. doctor remains the provider capability check.

Flags:
  --repo <path>             Repository (default: current repo)
  --json                    Emit structured health JSON instead of text
  --refresh                 Rebuild even when a matching index exists
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                            Index profile (default: full)
  --cache-dir <path>        Override the shared index cache directory
  --format text|json|auto   Report format (default: text)
  --head                    Accepted for symmetry; health always uses committed HEAD
  --no-network              Accepted for symmetry; health is always local-only
  --ignore-file <path>      Extra exclude rules (repeatable)
  --include-file <path>     Re-include ignored paths (repeatable)

Examples:
  entire graph health
  entire graph health --repo . --json
  entire graph health --refresh

content.content:
Usage:
  entire [flags]
  entire [command]

Entire Setup:
  agent                      Manage agent integrations (add, remove, list)
  clean                      Clean up Entire session data
  configure                  Update Entire settings in the current repository
  disable                    Disable Entire in current repository
  doctor                     Diagnose and fix session issues
  enable                     Enable Entire in current repository
  plugin                     Manage Entire plugins (install, list, upgrade, search, remove)
  status                     Show Entire status

Sessions & Checkpoints:
  activity                   Show your activity overview
  checkpoint                 Inspect and search checkpoints
  dispatch                   Generate a dispatch summarizing recent agent work
  recap                      Summarize recent checkpoint activity
  search                     Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
  session                    Manage agent sessions tracked by Entire

Trails:
  trail                      Manage trails across repositories and branches

Account:
  auth                       Manage authentication
  login                      Log in to Entire
  logout                     Log out of Entire

Control Plane:
  api                        Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
  cluster                    Show the Entire clusters you can place projects and repos on
  org                        Manage Entire organizations
  project                    Manage Entire projects
  repo                       Manage Entire repositories
  service-account            Manage project service accounts

Additional Commands:
  agent-help                 Machine-readable usage for coding agents (always matches the installed CLI)
entire plugin install — Install a plugin from the index, a git repository URL, or a local executable
Install a plugin.

Three source forms:

  name   Bare names resolve through the plugin index:
             entire plugin install run
  url    Full git repository URLs install from any git host. The newest
         semver tag is resolved with 'git ls-remote'; the platform's release
         asset is downloaded over HTTPS and verified against the release's
         checksums.txt. A release that publishes no checksums is refused
         unless --allow-unverified is passed:
             entire plugin install https://github.com/entireio/entire-run
  path   Local executables are linked into the managed directory (symlink
         first, so rebuilds are picked up immediately). Paths must be
         explicit — a separator or leading ./ — so a stray local file can
         never shadow an index name:
             entire plugin install ./dist/entire-run
             entire plugin install ./entire-run

Installing from a URL that is not listed in the plugin index asks for
confirmation; pass --yes to skip (required in non-interactive runs).

Plugins may declare dependencies in entire-plugin.yml. Missing dependencies
are listed and installed after a single confirmation (or with --yes);
--no-deps opts out.

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-vscode  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --allow-unverified[=true|false]   Install even when the release publishes no checksums.txt to authenticate the download
      --force[=true|false]              Replace an existing entry with the same name
      --index string                    Plugin index URL (overrides ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL and the built-in default)
      --no-deps[=true|false]            Do not install declared dependencies
      --pin string                      Install exactly this tag and skip it during 'plugin upgrade'
      --yes[=true|false]                Skip confirmation prompts (non-index sources, dependency installs)

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

content.content:
1	# Entire for VS Code
2	
3	Browse the [Entire](https://entire.com) checkpoints behind your commits, the agent sessions behind each checkpoint, and the trails of a repository on entire.com, in the editor where you read the code.
4	
5	![The Checkpoints and Sessions views in the sidebar, beside a checkpoint open in the detail panel with its files and transcript](images/checkpoint.png)
6	
7	## What You Get
8	
9	**Checkpoints view.** Lists each commit on the current branch that carries an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. One session produces a checkpoint for every commit made while it runs, so each row names the agent and says where its checkpoint sits in that session, such as 12 of 249. A commit expands only when there is something to tell apart: several checkpoints, as in a squash, or a checkpoint that holds several sessions. Checkpoints that no commit on the branch carries, such as imported ones, appear under Other Checkpoints. The list shows 50 commits at a time and loads the next 50 when you scroll to its end.
10	
11	**Sessions view.** Lists the sessions running now, then the rest by recency, each with its checkpoints under it. When the `origin` remote uses the `entire://` scheme, the view reads the repository's sessions from Entire, as the Sessions page of entire.com lists them: every session on every branch, under the name Entire gave it, with Entire's count of its checkpoints. Expanding a session lists the checkpoints your clone knows at once, and adds the ones Entire lists for it, such as those on other branches. In any other repository, a session appears when Entire has local state for it or when a checkpoint references it, and it is named by the prompt that opened it. The view loads 50 sessions at a time in the same way.
12	
13	**Detail panel.** Click a commit, checkpoint, or session to open it in an editor tab. The panel shows the commit, the files the session touched with a diff for each, and the transcript. Tool calls start collapsed, and expanding one shows its input and result. A checkpoint opens at its own part of the conversation, and Show Earlier Messages loads what came before. The panel says which checkpoint of the session it shows, and Previous and Next step through the session's other checkpoints. The selected row moves with the tab: the view you opened the tab from selects the row of the checkpoint the tab shows, and loads more of its list when that row is beyond the end.
14	
15	**Trails view.** Appears when the `origin` remote uses the `entire://` scheme. It lists the trails that touch the repository, most recent activity first, 50 at a time. Each row shows the trail's number, its phase, and its branch in this repository, and marks the trail whose branch you have checked out.
16	
17	A trail is open or closed, and an open trail is in a phase: planning, building, or complete. The filter button in the view's title bar shows only the trails in one of those states: All, Open, Closed, Planning, Building, or Complete. The view starts on Open and names the filter in use beside its title.
18	
19	**Trail panel.** Click a trail to open it in an editor tab. The panel shows the trail's description and its branches, which Entire calls changes. For a change it shows whether the branch can merge, each merge gate with the reason for its result, and the CI runs on the head commit. Below that is the change's timeline of commits, reviews, and resolved findings. A commit that is in your clone and carries a checkpoint has an Open Checkpoint button, which opens the session behind the commit in the detail panel.
20	
21	The panel fills in as the Entire CLI answers. It draws the title and status from the Trails view at once, then the changes, then the timeline. A trail you opened earlier in the same window shows from that read at once, and the panel reads it again and redraws what has changed.
22	
23	![The Trails and Brain views in the sidebar, beside a trail open in the trail panel with its merge gates, CI runs, and timeline](images/trail.png)
24	
25	**Links to entire.com.** When the `origin` remote uses the `entire://` scheme, each commit, session, and trail gets an Open on entire.com action.
26	
27	**Brain view.** The last section of the sidebar, shown when Entire is enabled in the repository and collapsed until you open it. It lists what the [entire-brain plugin](https://docs.entire.io/guides/brain/overview) reports about the repository's brain: whether it is built and when it was updated, the size of its code graph, its memories, conversations, and docs, whether it is up to date, whether background updates are running, and whether it is connected to a hosted brain. Anything that needs a look is marked, with the reason on hover. These details are text: only the section's buttons can be clicked.
28	
29	The View Brain button starts the plugin's graph page for the repository and opens it in your browser. The page draws the code entities in the brain and the calls and imports between them. The same button is in the section's title bar, and the command palette has Entire: View Brain. While the page's server runs, the section says where and has a Stop button. Closing the window stops it too.
30	
31	## Requirements
32	
33	- [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io/installation) 0.12.0 or later. The extension reads checkpoints and sessions through it.
34	- Git.
35	- A local repository with Entire enabled (`entire enable`), opened as a trusted workspace.
36	- For the Brain view, the entire-brain plugin (`entire plugin install brain`) and a brain for the repository (`entire brain setup`).
37	- For the Trails view, an `entire://` origin and a login saved with `entire login`. Trails are stored on Entire, not in the clone, so the view lists them whether or not Entire is enabled there.
38	- For session names from Entire, the same origin and login. Without them, the Sessions view names each session by its opening prompt.
39	
40	The extension looks for `entire` on your `PATH`, then in `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, and `/usr/local/bin`, and then asks your login shell. Set `entire.cliPath` if the binary lives somewhere else.
41	
42	## Getting Started
43	
44	1. Install the [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io/installation) and run `entire enable` in your repository.
45	2. Install Entire from the Extensions view in VS Code, Cursor, or another editor that installs from Open VSX.
46	3. Select the Entire icon in the activity bar.
47	
48	## Settings
49	
50	| Setting | Default | Purpose |
51	| --- | --- | --- |
52	| `entire.cliPath` | empty | Absolute path to the Entire CLI binary. |
53	| `entire.loadOnScroll` | `true` | Load the next 50 rows of a list when you scroll to its end. When off, click Load More. |
54	| `entire.trails.enabled` | `true` | Show the Trails view and read trails from Entire. When off, the view is hidden and the extension runs no `entire trail` command. |
55	| `entire.webBaseUrl` | empty | Base URL for links to the Entire web app. When empty, the extension uses `ENTIRE_WEB_BASE_URL` if it is set, and `https://entire.com` otherwise. |
56	
57	## What the Extension Runs
58	
59	The extension is a read-only explorer. It does not create, edit, or delete checkpoints, and it does not run `entire enable` for you. It runs these commands in your repository:
60	
61	| Command | When |
62	| --- | --- |
63	| `git log`, `git cat-file`, `git for-each-ref`, `git diff-tree` | To list commits, read stored transcripts, and build diffs. |
64	| `entire status --json` | On load and on each automatic refresh. |
65	| `entire checkpoint explain --json` | In the background, to add each checkpoint's agent and sessions to the views. |
66	| `entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>` | When you expand or open a checkpoint. |
67	| `entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id> --short` | When you open a checkpoint that no commit in the history read so far carries, to learn who its author is. Once for each such checkpoint. |
68	| `entire session list --json` | When the Sessions view is first shown, and when you click Refresh. |
69	| `entire api --to cell /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/sessions?scope=all&limit=50` | When the Sessions view is first shown, when its list loads the next page, and when you click Refresh. Only for an `entire://` origin. |
70	| `entire api --to cell /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/sessions/<session>/transcript` | When you expand or open a session for which Entire counts more checkpoints than your clone knows. Once for each such session, until you click Refresh. |
71	| `entire trail list --json` | When the Trails view is first shown, when you change the filter to another status, when the list loads its next page, and when you click Refresh. |
72	| `entire trail show <trail> --json` | When you open or refresh a trail, and the first time you open or copy a trail's link from its row. |
73	| `entire trail timeline <trail> --json` | When you open or refresh a trail, switch to another of its changes, or load more of its timeline. Opening a trail runs it once or twice: the panel asks for the trail's timeline while it reads the trail, and asks again for one change by name when the trail has several changes or a change whose branch is gone. |
74	| `entire brain status --json` | When the Brain view is first opened, when you click Refresh after that, and when you open the brain graph. |
75	| `entire brain viz --no-open --port 0` | When you open the brain graph and its server is not running for the repository. The plugin serves the page on 127.0.0.1 until you stop it or close the window. |
76	
77	Two of these have effects inside the Entire CLI. `entire checkpoint explain` fetches checkpoint data from your checkpoint remote when it is missing from the local clone. `entire session list` removes session state that has been idle for more than seven days, which is why the extension keeps it out of automatic refresh.
78

# Entire for VS Code

Browse the [Entire](https://entire.com) checkpoints behind your commits, the agent sessions behind each checkpoint, and the trails of a repository on entire.com, in the editor where you read the code.

![The Checkpoints and Sessions views in the sidebar, beside a checkpoint open in the detail panel with its files and transcript](images/checkpoint.png)

## What You Get

**Checkpoints view.** Lists each commit on the current branch that carries an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. One session produces a checkpoint for every commit made while it runs, so each row names the agent and says where its checkpoint sits in that session, such as 12 of 249. A commit expands only when there is something to tell apart: several checkpoints, as in a squash, or a checkpoint that holds several sessions. Checkpoints that no commit on the branch carries, such as imported ones, appear under Other Checkpoints. The list shows 50 commits at a time and loads the next 50 when you scroll to its end.

**Sessions view.** Lists the sessions running now, then the rest by recency, each with its checkpoints under it. When the `origin` remote uses the `entire://` scheme, the view reads the repository's sessions from Entire, as the Sessions page of entire.com lists them: every session on every branch, under the name Entire gave it, with Entire's count of its checkpoints. Expanding a session lists the checkpoints your clone knows at once, and adds the ones Entire lists for it, such as those on other branches. In any other repository, a session appears when Entire has local state for it or when a checkpoint references it, and it is named by the prompt that opened it. The view loads 50 sessions at a time in the same way.

**Detail panel.** Click a commit, checkpoint, or session to open it in an editor tab. The panel shows the commit, the files the session touched with a diff for each, and the transcript. Tool calls start collapsed, and expanding one shows its input and result. A checkpoint opens at its own part of the conversation, and Show Earlier Messages loads what came before. The panel says which checkpoint of the session it shows, and Previous and Next step through the session's other checkpoints. The selected row moves with the tab: the view you opened the tab from selects the row of the checkpoint the tab shows, and loads more of its list when that row is beyond the end.

**Trails view.** Appears when the `origin` remote uses the `entire://` scheme. It lists the trails that touch the repository, most recent activity first, 50 at a time. Each row shows the trail's number, its phase, and its branch in this repository, and marks the trail whose branch you have checked out.

A trail is open or closed, and an open trail is in a phase: planning, building, or complete. The filter button in the view's title bar shows only the trails in one of those states: All, Open, Closed, Planning, Building, or Complete. The view starts on Open and names the filter in use beside its title.

**Trail panel.** Click a trail to open it in an editor tab. The panel shows the trail's description and its branches, which Entire calls changes. For a change it shows whether the branch can merge, each merge gate with the reason for its result, and the CI runs on the head commit. Below that is the change's timeline of commits, reviews, and resolved findings. A commit that is in your clone and carries a checkpoint has an Open Checkpoint button, which opens the session behind the commit in the detail panel.

The panel fills in as the Entire CLI answers. It draws the title and status from the Trails view at once, then the changes, then the timeline. A trail you opened earlier in the same window shows from that read at once, and the panel reads it again and redraws what has changed.

![The Trails and Brain views in the sidebar, beside a trail open in the trail panel with its merge gates, CI runs, and timeline](images/trail.png)

**Links to entire.com.** When the `origin` remote uses the `entire://` scheme, each commit, session, and trail gets an Open on entire.com action.

**Brain view.** The last section of the sidebar, shown when Entire is enabled in the repository and collapsed until you open it. It lists what the [entire-brain plugin](https://docs.entire.io/guides/brain/overview) reports about the repository's brain: whether it is built and when it was updated, the size of its code graph, its memories, conversations, and docs, whether it is up to date, whether background updates are running, and whether it is connected to a hosted brain. Anything that needs a look is marked, with the reason on hover. These details are text: only the section's buttons can be clicked.

The View Brain button starts the plugin's graph page for the repository and opens it in your browser. The page draws the code entities in the brain and the calls and imports between them. The same button is in the section's title bar, and the command palette has Entire: View Brain. While the page's server runs, the section says where and has a Stop button. Closing the window stops it too.

## Requirements

- [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io/installation) 0.12.0 or later. The extension reads checkpoints and sessions through it.
- Git.
- A local repository with Entire enabled (`entire enable`), opened as a trusted workspace.
- For the Brain view, the entire-brain plugin (`entire plugin install brain`) and a brain for the repository (`entire brain setup`).
- For the Trails view, an `entire://` origin and a login saved with `entire login`. Trails are stored on Entire, not in the clone, so the view lists them whether or not Entire is enabled there.
- For session names from Entire, the same origin and login. Without them, the Sessions view names each session by its opening prompt.

The extension looks for `entire` on your `PATH`, then in `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, and `/usr/local/bin`, and then asks your login shell. Set `entire.cliPath` if the binary lives somewhere else.

## Getting Started

1. Install the [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io/installation) and run `entire enable` in your repository.
2. Install Entire from the Extensions view in VS Code, Cursor, or another editor that installs from Open VSX.
3. Select the Entire icon in the activity bar.

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entire.cliPath` | empty | Absolute path to the Entire CLI binary. |
| `entire.loadOnScroll` | `true` | Load the next 50 rows of a list when you scroll to its end. When off, click Load More. |
| `entire.trails.enabled` | `true` | Show the Trails view and read trails from Entire. When off, the view is hidden and the extension runs no `entire trail` command. |
| `entire.webBaseUrl` | empty | Base URL for links to the Entire web app. When empty, the extension uses `ENTIRE_WEB_BASE_URL` if it is set, and `https://entire.com` otherwise. |

## What the Extension Runs

The extension is a read-only explorer. It does not create, edit, or delete checkpoints, and it does not run `entire enable` for you. It runs these commands in your repository:

| Command | When |
| --- | --- |
| `git log`, `git cat-file`, `git for-each-ref`, `git diff-tree` | To list commits, read stored transcripts, and build diffs. |
| `entire status --json` | On load and on each automatic refresh. |
| `entire checkpoint explain --json` | In the background, to add each checkpoint's agent and sessions to the views. |
| `entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>` | When you expand or open a checkpoint. |
| `entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id> --short` | When you open a checkpoint that no commit in the history read so far carries, to learn who its author is. Once for each such checkpoint. |
| `entire session list --json` | When the Sessions view is first shown, and when you click Refresh. |
| `entire api --to cell /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/sessions?scope=all&limit=50` | When the Sessions view is first shown, when its list loads the next page, and when you click Refresh. Only for an `entire://` origin. |
| `entire api --to cell /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/sessions/<session>/transcript` | When you expand or open a session for which Entire counts more checkpoints than your clone knows. Once for each such session, until you click Refresh. |
| `entire trail list --json` | When the Trails view is first shown, when you change the filter to another status, when the list loads its next page, and when you click Refresh. |
| `entire trail show <trail> --json` | When you open or refresh a trail, and the first time you open or copy a trail's link from its row. |
| `entire trail timeline <trail> --json` | When you open or refresh a trail, switch to another of its changes, or load more of its timeline. Opening a trail runs it once or twice: the panel asks for the trail's timeline while it reads the trail, and asks again for one change by name when the trail has several changes or a change whose branch is gone. |
| `entire brain status --json` | When the Brain view is first opened, when you click Refresh after that, and when you open the brain graph. |
| `entire brain viz --no-open --port 0` | When you open the brain graph and its server is not running for the repository. The plugin serves the page on 127.0.0.1 until you stop it or close the window. |

Two of these have effects inside the Entire CLI. `entire checkpoint explain` fetches checkpoint data from your checkpoint remote when it is missing from the local clone. `entire session list` removes session state that has been idle for more than seven days, which is why the extension keeps it out of automatic refresh.

The extension sends no network requests of its own. The three trail commands and the two `entire api` calls make the Entire CLI read Entire over the network with your saved login. The extension runs them only for a repository whose `origin` uses the `entire://` scheme, and not before the view that needs them is on screen. It runs none of the trail commands that write, such as `entire trail approve` or `entire trail merge`.

`entire api` is the CLI's authenticated request to Entire's API. The extension gives it a path and nothing else, which makes it a GET: it passes no method, field, or body. The CLI calls these endpoints internal and says their shape can change without notice. When a read fails, or returns something the extension does not recognize, the Sessions view shows what your clone knows, with each session named by its opening prompt.

The brain graph is served on your machine by the entire-brain plugin, on the loopback address. The plugin describes the page as read-only, with no outbound network. The extension opens only that local address.

Open Raw Transcript has the Entire CLI write the transcript to a file in a private temporary directory, opens it read-only, and removes it when the window closes. A raw transcript can run to hundreds of megabytes, so it goes to a file instead of through memory.

## Limits

- Loading on scroll pauses when it reads 20,000 commits without finding a checkpoint. Click Load More Checkpoints to read further back.
- A commit can name a checkpoint whose session data was never uploaded. The commit carries the checkpoint's ID, and the Entire CLI uploads the data separately. Opening one shows the commit and its diff with a note in place of the transcript, and its row then reads "no session data".
- A session with no checkpoint yet shows its facts and its raw transcript, with no chat view.
- The selected row follows a tab only in the view the tab was opened from, and only while that view is on screen. The other view keeps its own selection. A tab opened from a trail is followed by the Checkpoints view. A tab opened on a session's own row has no Previous and Next, so its selection stays on the session.
- Session names come from Entire only for an `entire://` origin and a saved login. The view reads them when it is first shown and when you click Refresh, and it does not follow changes on Entire in between. A session that Entire has not listed yet, such as one that is still running, is named as in any other repository until then.
- Without Entire's list, a session's name is read from the start of the normalized transcript that its checkpoints store. A session with no checkpoint shows its latest prompt in its place. A session whose checkpoints store no normalized transcript, as some Codex sessions do not, shows the message of its newest checkpoint until you open it, and its opening prompt after that.
- Entire's count of a session's checkpoints can be higher than the number its page on entire.com lists. In testing, a session counted at 36 listed 29. A session's row shows the count until you expand it, and the number of checkpoints listed after that.
- Entire sends a session's checkpoints with its transcript. In testing that took two to eight seconds, so the checkpoints your clone knows show first and the rest are added when they arrive.
- Entire can list a checkpoint whose session data the Entire CLI cannot find in your clone or on the checkpoint remote. Opening one shows a note in place of the transcript, and Open on entire.com shows the session there.
- A transcript does not record who sent its prompts. The panel names the author of the commit that carries the checkpoint, as the Entire CLI does. For a checkpoint with no commit in the history read so far, it names the author the CLI reports, which arrives a moment after the transcript. A prompt reads "User" when neither is known.
- The chat view reads the normalized transcript that Entire stores in each checkpoint. A session without one falls back to the Entire CLI's text view, which omits tool inputs and results and covers the latest session of a checkpoint.

Older commits show commit details until you open them. A plus sign, as in 210+, marks a session at the old end of that list, which may have earlier checkpoints.

1	# Contributing
2	
3	## Development
4	
5	Node 22.18 or later is required.
6	
7	```sh
8	npm install
9	npm run build                      # bundle the extension and the panel into dist/
10	npm run check                      # lint, type-check, and unit tests
11	npm run test:host                  # run the extension in a VS Code instance against a fixture repository
12	npm run smoke -- /path/to/repo     # print what the extension would show for a real repository
13	npm run notices                    # rewrite THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md after a bundled dependency changes
14	```
15	
16	Press F5 in VS Code to start an Extension Development Host with the extension loaded.
17	
18	The extension-host tests open real editor windows, one per launch, and close them when they finish. The windows start with Chromium's background throttling turned off, because they usually sit behind your other windows and the editor slows down there.
19	
20	The extension-host tests run in VS Code by default. To run them in another editor built on VS Code, point `ENTIRE_TEST_EDITOR` at its executable. Each launch uses a profile of its own, so the editor's real settings and extensions are left alone.
21	
22	```sh
23	ENTIRE_TEST_EDITOR=/Applications/Cursor.app/Contents/MacOS/Cursor npm run test:host
24	npx vscode-test --code-version 1.95.0    # the oldest VS Code the manifest allows
25	```
26	
27	## Layout
28	
29	| Path | Contents |
30	| --- | --- |
31	| `src/core` | Git and Entire CLI logic. It does not import `vscode`, so it runs under plain Node in tests. |
32	| `src/ext` | Tree views, commands, file watchers, and the panel hosts. |
33	| `src/webview` | The UI of the detail panel and the trail panel, bundled separately for the browser. One bundle serves both, and the host says which page to draw. |
34	| `src/shared` | Message types that the host and the panels both use. |
35	| `test/unit`, `test/webview` | `vitest` tests. Webview tests run on `happy-dom`, except the Markdown sanitizer tests and the trail panel tests, which need `jsdom` because DOMPurify does not work on `happy-dom`. |
36	| `test/integration` | Tests that run inside a VS Code extension host. |
37	| `test/fake-entire` | A stand-in for the Entire CLI that replays canned output. |
38	
39	Ten things are easy to break without noticing:
40	
41	- Automatic refresh calls `entire status --json` and git only. `entire session list` prunes old session state, so it runs when the Sessions view is first shown and on a manual refresh. An extension-host test asserts this.
42	- A list loads its next page when its Load More row scrolls into view. Tree views report nothing about scrolling, so `src/ext/views/scrollLoader.ts` relies on the editor asking for a row's file decoration when it draws the row. The row's `resourceUri` is what makes that work, and the extension-host tests in `test/integration/scroll.test.cjs` fail if an editor stops asking that way.
43	- The selected row follows the detail tab (`src/ext/views/selectionSync.ts`). A click selects a row, but Previous and Next move the tab without a click, and `TreeView.reveal` is the only way to move a selection. `reveal` takes a row object and looks for it among the ones the editor was given. An equal row that is another object is not found, and VS Code 1.95 refuses it as a duplicate. So the Checkpoints and Sessions trees hand out one object for each row ID and update it in place (`src/ext/views/rowRegistry.ts`). Do not return a freshly built row from `getChildren` past the registry, and do not keep a row object to compare its old fields with later ones. `reveal` also opens the sidebar on a view that is hidden, so a view that is not visible is left alone. The tests in `test/integration/extension.test.cjs` run against a real tree view, and are worth running on the oldest supported editor after a change here.
44	- A raw transcript goes from the CLI straight to a temporary file (`src/ext/transcriptFiles.ts`), not into memory. One long session's transcript measured 178 MB. Open such files with the `vscode.open` command: the extension host refuses to load documents over 50 MB.
45	- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` is the only module that knows how checkpoints are stored in git. It exists to read the normalized transcript, which no CLI command outputs, and every reader in it falls back to the CLI on a surprise. The transcript is read whole to show it, and its first lines are read to name a session by its opening prompt. Most transcripts hold the session from its start, so each checkpoint of a session gives the same opening prompt. A transcript with no start line holds only its checkpoint's part, and its first prompt is not taken for the session's unless the checkpoint is the session's first.
46	- Trails and Entire's session list are the two features that reach the network. Trails go through `entire trail list`, `show`, and `timeline`. Those three only read. The other trail commands write, and the extension runs none of them. Nothing calls the three until the Trails view is on screen, which `test/integration/states.test.cjs` asserts, and nothing calls them while the `entire.trails.enabled` setting is off, which `test/integration/trails.test.cjs` asserts. A trail's web address comes from `entire trail show`, because the CLI asks callers not to build one. The CLI lists trails by status only, so `src/core/trails.ts` matches a phase filter against the trails read so far and limits how many pages one load may read.
47	- The Sessions view takes its names from Entire's API, through `entire api --to cell` (`src/core/remoteSessions.ts`, and `remoteSessions` and `remoteSessionCheckpoints` in `src/core/entireCli.ts`). The calls pass a path and no other flag, so the CLI sends a GET, and a test in `test/unit/remoteSessionsCli.test.ts` fails if a method, field, or body flag appears. The CLI calls these endpoints internal, so the readers take only the fields they know and every failure falls back to what the clone knows: the session list from the CLI and git, with names from stored transcripts. The API answers a refusal as JSON on stdout with a non-zero exit, which is why these calls do not use `jsonResult`. Nothing reads the list until the Sessions view is on screen, and automatic refresh never reads it, which `test/integration/extension.test.cjs` and `test/integration/states.test.cjs` assert. A session's checkpoints come with its whole transcript, so that call runs only for a session whose count on Entire exceeds what the clone knows, once, and the rows the clone knows are drawn without waiting for it.
48	- The trail panel reads a trail and its timeline side by side, because each call takes seconds (`src/ext/panel/trailPanelController.ts`). Until the trail is read, the timeline call can name only the trail, and the CLI then picks the change without saying which one it read. The panel uses that answer only when the trail has one change, and asks for the change by name otherwise. The CLI picks by branch, so it refuses a change whose branch is gone, and the panel asks for such a change by name without waiting for the refusal. `test/integration/trails.test.cjs` has a trail for each case. What the panel keeps in `src/core/trailMemory.ts` is a head start: it reads a trail again each time it draws one from there.
49	- The brain graph is a server that the extension starts and has to stop (`src/ext/brainService.ts`, `src/core/serverProcess.ts`). `entire brain viz` runs until it is stopped, as a child of the Entire CLI, so the extension stops the whole process group, and it stops every server when the window closes. The plugin's page forbids framing, which is why it opens in the browser and not in a panel. # Contributing

## Development

Node 22.18 or later is required.

```sh
npm install
npm run build                      # bundle the extension and the panel into dist/
npm run check                      # lint, type-check, and unit tests
npm run test:host                  # run the extension in a VS Code instance against a fixture repository
npm run smoke -- /path/to/repo     # print what the extension would show for a real repository
npm run notices                    # rewrite THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md after a bundled dependency changes
```

Press F5 in VS Code to start an Extension Development Host with the extension loaded.

The extension-host tests open real editor windows, one per launch, and close them when they finish. The windows start with Chromium's background throttling turned off, because they usually sit behind your other windows and the editor slows down there.

The extension-host tests run in VS Code by default. To run them in another editor built on VS Code, point `ENTIRE_TEST_EDITOR` at its executable. Each launch uses a profile of its own, so the editor's real settings and extensions are left alone.

```sh
ENTIRE_TEST_EDITOR=/Applications/Cursor.app/Contents/MacOS/Cursor npm run test:host
npx vscode-test --code-version 1.95.0    # the oldest VS Code the manifest allows
```

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `src/core` | Git and Entire CLI logic. It does not import `vscode`, so it runs under plain Node in tests. |
| `src/ext` | Tree views, commands, file watchers, and the panel hosts. |
| `src/webview` | The UI of the detail panel and the trail panel, bundled separately for the browser. One bundle serves both, and the host says which page to draw. |
| `src/shared` | Message types that the host and the panels both use. |
| `test/unit`, `test/webview` | `vitest` tests. Webview tests run on `happy-dom`, except the Markdown sanitizer tests and the trail panel tests, which need `jsdom` because DOMPurify does not work on `happy-dom`. |
| `test/integration` | Tests that run inside a VS Code extension host. |
| `test/fake-entire` | A stand-in for the Entire CLI that replays canned output. |

Ten things are easy to break without noticing:

- Automatic refresh calls `entire status --json` and git only. `entire session list` prunes old session state, so it runs when the Sessions view is first shown and on a manual refresh. An extension-host test asserts this.
- A list loads its next page when its Load More row scrolls into view. Tree views report nothing about scrolling, so `src/ext/views/scrollLoader.ts` relies on the editor asking for a row's file decoration when it draws the row. The row's `resourceUri` is what makes that work, and the extension-host tests in `test/integration/scroll.test.cjs` fail if an editor stops asking that way.
- The selected row follows the detail tab (`src/ext/views/selectionSync.ts`). A click selects a row, but Previous and Next move the tab without a click, and `TreeView.reveal` is the only way to move a selection. `reveal` takes a row object and looks for it among the ones the editor was given. An equal row that is another object is not found, and VS Code 1.95 refuses it as a duplicate. So the Checkpoints and Sessions trees hand out one object for each row ID and update it in place (`src/ext/views/rowRegistry.ts`). Do not return a freshly built row from `getChildren` past the registry, and do not keep a row object to compare its old fields with later ones. `reveal` also opens the sidebar on a view that is hidden, so a view that is not visible is left alone. The tests in `test/integration/extension.test.cjs` run against a real tree view, and are worth running on the oldest supported editor after a change here.
- A raw transcript goes from the CLI straight to a temporary file (`src/ext/transcriptFiles.ts`), not into memory. One long session's transcript measured 178 MB. Open such files with the `vscode.open` command: the extension host refuses to load documents over 50 MB.
- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` is the only module that knows how checkpoints are stored in git. It exists to read the normalized transcript, which no CLI command outputs, and every reader in it falls back to the CLI on a surprise. The transcript is read whole to show it, and its first lines are read to name a session by its opening prompt. Most transcripts hold the session from its start, so each checkpoint of a session gives the same opening prompt. A transcript with no start line holds only its checkpoint's part, and its first prompt is not taken for the session's unless the checkpoint is the session's first.
- Trails and Entire's session list are the two features that reach the network. Trails go through `entire trail list`, `show`, and `timeline`. Those three only read. The other trail commands write, and the extension runs none of them. Nothing calls the three until the Trails view is on screen, which `test/integration/states.test.cjs` asserts, and nothing calls them while the `entire.trails.enabled` setting is off, which `test/integration/trails.test.cjs` asserts. A trail's web address comes from `entire trail show`, because the CLI asks callers not to build one. The CLI lists trails by status only, so `src/core/trails.ts` matches a phase filter against the trails read so far and limits how many pages one load may read.
- The Sessions view takes its names from Entire's API, through `entire api --to cell` (`src/core/remoteSessions.ts`, and `remoteSessions` and `remoteSessionCheckpoints` in `src/core/entireCli.ts`). The calls pass a path and no other flag, so the CLI sends a GET, and a test in `test/unit/remoteSessionsCli.test.ts` fails if a method, field, or body flag appears. The CLI calls these endpoints internal, so the readers take only the fields they know and every failure falls back to what the clone knows: the session list from the CLI and git, with names from stored transcripts. The API answers a refusal as JSON on stdout with a non-zero exit, which is why these calls do not use `jsonResult`. Nothing reads the list until the Sessions view is on screen, and automatic refresh never reads it, which `test/integration/extension.test.cjs` and `test/integration/states.test.cjs` assert. A session's checkpoints come with its whole transcript, so that call runs only for a session whose count on Entire exceeds what the clone knows, once, and the rows the clone knows are drawn without waiting for it.
- The trail panel reads a trail and its timeline side by side, because each call takes seconds (`src/ext/panel/trailPanelController.ts`). Until the trail is read, the timeline call can name only the trail, and the CLI then picks the change without saying which one it read. The panel uses that answer only when the trail has one change, and asks for the change by name otherwise. The CLI picks by branch, so it refuses a change whose branch is gone, and the panel asks for such a change by name without waiting for the refusal. `test/integration/trails.test.cjs` has a trail for each case. What the panel keeps in `src/core/trailMemory.ts` is a head start: it reads a trail again each time it draws one from there.
- The brain graph is a server that the extension starts and has to stop (`src/ext/brainService.ts`, `src/core/serverProcess.ts`). `entire brain viz` runs until it is stopped, as a child of the Entire CLI, so the extension stops the whole process group, and it stops every server when the window closes. The plugin's page forbids framing, which is why it opens in the browser and not in a panel. The address the extension opens is rebuilt from the port in the plugin's ready line (`parseVizUrl` in `src/core/brain.ts`) and is never that line's text. Nothing runs a brain command until the Brain view, which starts collapsed, is opened or View Brain is used. `test/integration/states.test.cjs` asserts that in windows whose sidebar stays closed. That file's fake server prints an address and serves nothing, so run the command against a real brain after a change here.
- The Brain view is a page and not a tree (`src/core/brainPage.ts`, `src/ext/views/brainView.ts`). Every row of a tree view looks clickable, and the brain's details are text with nothing to click. The page has no script. Its buttons are links to commands, and the view lets the editor run only the commands in `BRAIN_PAGE_COMMANDS`. A row that does nothing does not belong in a tree view: put it on a page, or leave it out.

## Screenshots

The two pictures in `images/` are of the extension in VS Code, on a demo repository with made-up commits, sessions, and trails. The fake Entire CLI in `test/fake-entire` supplies the data, as it does for the extension-host tests. Retake them when a view changes, and take them from made-up data: a screenshot of a real repository publishes its session names, prompts, and transcripts.

The README links to them by relative path. `vsce` rewrites those links to this repository on GitHub when it packages the extension, so the pictures are not in the VSIX, and they show on the Marketplace only while the repository is public.

## Releasing

A release is a tag. Pushing `v<version>` runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which builds the VSIX once and publishes that one file to the Visual Studio Marketplace, to Open VSX, and to a GitHub release for the tag. The release takes its notes from the version's entry in `CHANGELOG.md`, and its VSIX is the file to install by hand with Extensions: Install from VSIX.

1. Update `version` in `package.json` and add an entry to `CHANGELOG.md`.
2. Run `npm run check`, `npm run test:host`, and `npm run package`. The last command writes `entire-<version>.vsix`.
3. Install that file with `code --install-extension entire-<version>.vsix` and open a repository that has checkpoints.
4. Commit, then tag and push the tag: `git tag v<version>` and `git push origin v<version>`.

### One-Time Setup

**Visual Studio Marketplace.** The workflow signs in with [GitHub Trusted Publishing](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/working-with-extensions/publishing-extension), so the repository stores no Marketplace token. The personal access tokens that `vsce` used before are retired on December 1, 2026.

1. Create the publisher `entire` at [marketplace.visualstudio.com/manage](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/manage). Its ID has to match `publisher` in `package.json`, and it cannot be changed later.
2. Open the publisher, select Trusted Publishing, and create a policy with repository owner `entireio`, repository `entire-vscode`, workflow `release.yml`, and environment `marketplace`.

**Open VSX.** The steps are in the [Open VSX publishing guide](https://github.com/eclipse/openvsx/wiki/Publishing-Extensions).

1. Create an Eclipse account, sign in to open-vsx.org with GitHub, and accept the Publisher Agreement in the profile settings.
2. Generate an access token under Settings, Access Tokens, and create the namespace with `npx ovsx create-namespace entire -p <token>`.
3. Save the token as the secret `OVSX_PAT` in the repository's `open-vsx` environment.

The two publish jobs run in the `marketplace` and `open-vsx` environments. Add required reviewers to them in the repository settings if a release should wait for an approval.
